title: SAY THIS POWERFUL PSALM 46 PROPHETIC MORNING DECLARATION PRAYER EVERY MORNING
text: Hallelujah. Glory to God. I want to take a moment before we go anywhere before I open my mouth to say anything to just acknowledge the presence of the one who makes all of this possible. Holy Spirit, you are welcome here. You are not [music] a doctrine to us. You are not a concept we inherited from a theological classroom. You are a person. You are the most important person in this room, in this space, in this moment. And we yield to you. We surrender the next moments to your sovereign agenda. Have your way, Lord. Have your way. Father, I thank you for every life connected to this word. I thank you that you do not waste a moment. You do not allow your children to stumble [music] into encounters accidentally. Every person hearing this voice right now was ordained to hear it at this hour. So, let your word do the work that sermons [music] cannot do. Let the anointing break the yoke in Jesus' name. Amen. Now, I want you to open your Bible or open your heart if you do not have a physical Bible with you to Psalm 46. Psalm 46. And I want you to read it slowly. Not as a reader reads literature, not as a student reads an assignment. I want you to read it the way a drowning man reads the word that tells him there is a shore. Because somebody hearing me right now, that is exactly where you are. You are not in a casual season. You are in a season where the waters have risen. And God in his infinite wisdom placed this psalm in the cannon of scripture specifically for moments like the one you are navigating. Psalm 46 verse one. God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Verse two, therefore we will not fear even though the earth be removed and though the mountains be carried into the midst of the sea. Verse three, though its waters roar and be troubled, though the mountains shake with its swelling. Verse four, there is a river whose streams shall make glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacle of the most high. Verse five, God is in the midst of her. She shall not be moved. God shall help her just at the break [music] of dawn. Verse six, the nations raged, the kingdoms were moved. He uttered his voice, the earth melted. Verse seven, the Lord of hosts is with us. The God of Jacob is our refuge. Verse 8, come behold the works of the Lord who has made dissolations in the earth. Verse 9, he makes wars to cease to the end of the earth. He breaks the bow and cuts the spear in two. He burns the chariot in the fire. Verse 10, be still and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations. I'll be exalted in the earth. Verse 11, the Lord of hosts is with us. The God of Jacob is our refuge. Hear me. Hear me this morning. I need you to understand that you just read one of the most militantly tender passages in all of scripture. It is militantly tender. It is fierce and it is gentle. It is like a strong man holding a child. It is like a warrior singing a lullaby over a battlefield. And the reason the Holy Spirit is directing us here this morning is because somebody in this place needs both dimensions. You need the strength of the warrior God and you need the tenderness of the father God. And Psalm 46 gives you both in 11 verses. Now this psalm was written by the sons of Kora. This is important. The sons of Kora were Levitical singers. [music] They were men who lived in proximity to the presence. Their entire inheritance, their entire vocational calling was wrapped up in the ministry of worship and intercession. These were not men who wrote from a distance. These were not theologians who sat in libraries and theorized about God. These were men who had stood in the courts of the Lord, who had felt the wind of the spirit move through the curtain of the tabernacle, who had watched the glory descend and fill the holy place. These men knew what they were talking about. And when they write, "God is our refuge and strength." They are not giving you a theological proposition. They are giving you a testimony. I need to stop here because this is where I think we lose the weight of scripture. We read these verses like they are bumper sticker theology. God is our refuge and strength. We put it on a coffee mug. We put it in a WhatsApp status. But this man wrote this from inside a crisis. Somebody hear me. This psalm was most likely written in the context of a national threat. Possibly the Syrian invasion under Senakarib when the armies of the greatest military power on earth surrounded Jerusalem and the people of God were hemmed in on every side. It was written when the mountains were literally shaking, metaphorically speaking, when everything that was stable appeared to be crumbling. And out of that context, out of that pressure, out of that midnight, comes this declaration. God is our refuge and strength. I am preaching to somebody this morning. The thing that you are calling the worst season of your life may actually be the very furnace that is forging the most powerful testimony of your life. You do not find out that God is a refuge when you are comfortable. You do not discover that he's a very present help when there is no trouble. It takes trouble to prove the presence. It takes the storm to reveal the anchor. And what is happening to you right now, as terrifying as it feels, as overwhelming as the sound of it is, as high as the water has risen, is simply the context in which God is about to show up as a very present help. Now look at that phrase, a very present help in trouble. I love the specificity of this. It does not say a distant help. It does not say an eventual help. It does not say a help that will arrive after you have exhausted every other option. It says a very present help. The word very is an intensifier. It is there to eliminate your doubt about the nearness of God in the moment of crisis. God is not watching your situation from a balcony. God is not observing your breakdown from a comfortable distance. God is present. He is very present. He is present in the way oxygen [music] is present. You cannot see it but you are breathing it. You cannot hold it but without it you have nothing. God is that present in your trouble. This is important. Most people's theology of God becomes small in seasons of trial. When things are going well, we can speak eloquently about the sovereignty and the nearness of God. But the moment the diagnosis comes, the moment the relationship collapses, the moment the business fails, the moment the child walks away, suddenly our theology shrinks. Suddenly God feels far. Suddenly prayer feels like it is bouncing off the ceiling. Suddenly we wonder if he has forgotten us, if he has moved on, if perhaps we disqualified ourselves from his intervention. And the spirit of God wants to arrest that mentality this morning. He is a very present help in trouble. The word trouble in the Hebrew carries the idea of tight places, distress, constriction. The image is of a narrow path hemmed in on both sides. And God is saying even there even in the tightest place you have ever been squeezed into I am there. I was there before you arrived I will be there when you emerge and I will be there in every moment of the constriction itself. Therefore the psalmist says we will not fear. Not we cannot fear. Not we do not feel the trembling. Not we are somehow robotically immune to the emotional weight of crisis. He says we will not. This is a decision. Fear is an emotion, but yielding to fear is a choice. And the psalmist is telling you that the antidote to fear is not the absence of danger. The antidote to fear is the revelation of God's presence in the danger when you know he is there. Truly know it. Not as a cliche but as a living reality. The fear loses its authority over your choices. Verse two gives you the extremity of the [music] promise. Even though the earth be removed, even if the mountains fall into the sea, even in the most catastrophically unimaginable scenario, we will not fear. I want you to feel the scope of that. God is not saying I will protect you from small inconveniences. God is saying even in cosmic level upheaval, I am still your refuge. Even if everything you trusted in, everything you built on, every human foundation crumbles beneath your feet, I remain. I am the rock that cannot be [music] removed. I am the mountain that does not shake. Now, I need to come here for a moment because verse four introduces something that most people miss when they read this psalm quickly. There is a river. There is a river in the middle of a psalm about mountains being cast into the sea, about waters roaring and being troubled, about kingdoms raging and the earth melting. Suddenly, the psalmist says, "But there is a river whose streams make [music] glad the city of God." Do you see the contrast? Outside the city, chaos, roaring waters, shaking mountains, raging nations. But inside, inside the city of God, inside the dwelling place of the most high, there is a river of gladness. There is a river that does not roar in terror, but streams in peace. Hear me. Your prayer life is that river. Your intimacy with the Holy Spirit is that river. Your time in the presence of God every morning like this morning is you positioning yourself inside the [music] city where the river flows. And you need to understand that the storms do not stop because you enter the city. The chaos outside does not immediately cease the moment you enter the presence. But inside there is a stream. Inside there is a source of gladness that has nothing to do with your external circumstances. The gladness that God gives is not circumstantial. [music] It is not produced by good news. It is not dependent on the economy, on your health report, on what your enemies are or are not doing. It is a river. Rivers flow from a source and the source is God himself. This is why David in another psalm says, "You will show me the path of life. In your presence is fullness of joy. At your right hand are pleasures forever more." The joy is in the presence. And if you have access to the presence, you have access to the joy. Regardless of what season you are in, I am preaching to somebody who has been trying to find joy in the resolution of your problem. And God is saying, "Stop looking there. The joy is not in the resolution. The joy is in the relationship. Come into my presence. Let the river make you glad." And then from that place of gladness, watch how I handle what is outside the walls. Verse five, God is in the midst of her. She shall not be moved. God shall help her. Just at the break of dawn. Just at the break of dawn. Oh, I love this. I love this. This phrase is almost too tender for me to preach without losing my composure. Just at the break of dawn. The implication is that there was a night. There was a night of trouble. There was a night of roaring waters and shaking mountains. There was a night when it seemed like the enemy would prevail. But God's help did not come at the beginning of the night. It came at the break of dawn. Weeping endures for a night, but joy comes in the morning, for the Lord of hosts is with us. Somebody is in a night season and you have been in it long enough that you have started to wonder if morning is real. You have started to question whether the dawn actually comes after your particular kind of darkness. And the spirit of the Lord wants me to tell you with the authority of this ancient text, morning is coming. Your morning is coming. And God's help will arrive just [music] at the break of dawn. Not a moment late. Not after you have given up. Not after you have made a decision based on the assumption that he was not coming. Just at the break of dawn. Hold on. Just hold on. Now before we move into the declarations and the warfare, I want to pause and do something. I want to obey the prompings of the spirit because there is someone hearing this word and it is not just for you. There is someone in your circle, someone you know, a friend, a family member, a colleague, someone whose number you have not dialed in a while, who is in a night season worse than anything you are currently facing. And the Holy Spirit is saying, "Be a carrier. Be a vessel. Send this word. Share it. Forward it. Whatever you need to do in this generation to get this into the ears of that person, do it. Do not let selfishness or passivity keep a breakthrough from someone who is waiting for the very thing God poured into this moment. You are a distributor of revival. Act like it now. Now we shift. Something is changing in this atmosphere. I feel the spirit of God moving from the gentle instruction of the teacher to the authority of the prophet. And I need you to shift with me. Straighten up on the inside. Get your spiritual attention because what I am about to declare over your life is not my opinion. It is the verdict of heaven concerning your situation. Thus says the Lord to you, the one reading this, the one whose ears are receiving this sound, whose spirit is open to this world. You are not forgotten. You are not an afterthought in the kingdom of God. The silence you have experienced was not neglect. The delay you have endured was not rejection. God is in the midst of your situation and she shall not be moved. Hear me. You shall not be moved. You will not be moved by this diagnosis. You will [music] not be moved by this financial pressure. You will not be moved by what your enemies are saying in the corridors where you cannot hear them. You will not be moved by the rejection of men because the acceptance of God is the only currency that matters in the economy of eternity. I declare over your life this morning that the mountains of impossibility that have stood in your path shall be carried into the sea. Every obstacle that has set to your destiny this far and no further. I decree that the word of God is dismantling it even now. Even now, not tomorrow. Not at the end of this season. Even as this word goes forth, the sovereign hand of God is rearranging the landscape of your life in your favor. The nations raged. The kingdoms were moved. He uttered his voice and the earth melted. God does not negotiate with your enemies. God does not debate with the powers that have been assigned against your destiny. He speaks once and the earth melts. He speaks once and the assignment is terminated. And he's speaking over your life this morning. I declare that the river of God is touching your home. That river that makes glad the city of God is flowing through your household. There is healing flowing in that river. There is restoration flowing in that river. There is provision flowing in that river. There is peace flowing in that river. A peace that surpasses the understanding of every person in your household. A peace that settles on every member of your family even before they understand what [music] is happening. The river is touching your home. I prophesy to you that the dawn is breaking over your situation. The night of weeping is giving way to the morning of joy. And the help of God is arriving just at the break of dawn, just in time, with precision, with accuracy, with the thoroughess that only an omnisient God can bring. His help is not partial. His help is not a temporary patch. His help is comprehensive, covering every dimension of what you have lost, restoring every year that the locust consumed, making up for every moment of delay with the supernatural acceleration that only the Lord of hosts can [music] provide. I declare that you are the city of God. You are the dwelling place of the most high. And because God is in the midst of you, you shall not be moved. Say it to yourself. Say it under your breath. I shall not be moved. Say it again. I shall not be moved. Not by the economy, not by the doctor's report, not by the disappointment, not by the betrayal, not by the loneliness, not by the fear. I shall not be moved because God is in the midst of me and he has never lost a battle and he does not intend to start with mine. I decree that the bow is broken. Every weapon that was drawn and aimed at your future, I declare that the Lord of Hosts is breaking it even now. He breaks the bow, he cuts the spear in two, he burns the chariot in the fire. Everything that the enemy assembled against you, every strategy, every coordinated attack, every systematic assignment of darkness against your destiny, God is dismantling it with the fire of his word. They thought they had the superior weapon. They did not account for the Lord of hosts showing up. And he's here. He's here. I declare fruitfulness over your labor. What your hands have been touching, what your mind has been working on, what your spirit has been pressing toward, I speak the blessing of God over it. Increase, multiplication, overflow. That which was withheld is being released. Doors that were shut by the hand of the enemy are being opened by the hand of God. Doors that no man can shutting wide open before you. Isaiah 60 says, "Arise and shine for your light has [music] come and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you. Your light has come. Your season of arising is here and now now we go to war. Now we enter the place of militant intercession because it is not enough to declare what God has said if we do not press it into the spirit realm with the violence of prayer." Jesus said, "The kingdom of heaven suffers violence and the violent take it by force. We are not casual participants in the affairs of our destiny. We are violent intercessors. We are people who have understood that prayer is not a ritual of religion. Prayer is the engagement of a citizen of heaven with the government of eternity. And we are pressing in now. Father, I come before you in the name that is above every other name. The name of Jesus. The name at which every knee bows in heaven and on earth and under the earth. The name that makes demons flee. The name that silences the roaring seas. The name that shook the prison where Paul and Silas were chained at midnight. I come before you in that name. And I am not coming on behalf of myself alone. I am coming on behalf of everyone whose spirit is engaged with this word. Everyone who opened their eyes this morning carrying a weight they did not know how to put down. Everyone who woke up to a situation that has not changed, I am standing in the gap. I am standing between them and the [music] assignment of darkness that has been pressing against their lives. Lord of hosts, I invoke your name this morning. Not the Lord of suggestions, not the Lord of possibilities, the Lord of hosts, the Lord of armies, the God who [music] commands legions of angels, who arrays the hosts of heaven like a commander arrays his troops. Lord of hosts, you are our refuge. And I am running to you this morning on behalf of every person under the sound of this prayer. Father, I pray against every spirit of fear that has been operating in the lives of those hearing this word. Fear that comes at night. Fear that comes in the morning when consciousness returns before grace returns. Fear that whispers [music] this is too much. Fear that says you are too far behind to catch up. Fear that says God has forgotten you. I bind that spirit in the name of Jesus. I command it to lose its grip. I command it to release its strangle hold on the minds and the hearts and the emotions of every person connected to this moment. The spirit of God does not give a spirit of fear. He gives power and love and a sound mind. Power, love, a sound mind. I receive that on behalf of every listener. Power to navigate this season. Love to sustain the heart through the loneliness. a sound mind to think clearly, to make the right decisions, to discern the voice of God even when everything [music] is noisy. I pray against every spirit of discouragement. Lord, the enemy knows that if he can make a person lose heart, he wins without a fight. So, he engineers situations. [music] He stacks disappointments. He times setbacks. He makes it seem like every time you take one step forward, something pushes you three steps back. He manufactures the feeling of futility. And Lord, I destroy that assignment right now in the name of Jesus. I decree that the hearts of those hearing this are being strengthened. Let not their hearts be troubled. Let not their hearts be afraid. Let the God of all comfort, the Father of mercies, pour his comfort into every broken place. Let him be found as a very present help in this trouble, this very moment. As this prayer ascends, I stand against every golad, every giant that has been taunting the armies of the living God, every situation that has been saying, "Nobody can fix this. Nobody can change this. This is permanent. This is your lot. This is as good as it gets." I decree that the God of David who took a shepherd boy with a sling and a stone and brought down the most feared warrior in the region, that same God is arising on behalf of those who are facing giants today. The giant shall fall, it shall fall face forward, face forward, not backward. The giant shall fall in the direction of where you have been advancing toward. And when it falls, you will take its head and you will carry it as a trophy of the faithfulness of God. Father, I pray specifically for those facing health crisis. For those who receive the reports that the enemy intended to use as a death sentence. [music] I stand against that word. I counter it with the word of God. By his stripes, we are healed. That is not poetry. That is covenant language. That is a legal declaration made at Calvary that has never been revoked and can never be revoked. Every sickness, every disease, every infirmity that has set up residence in a body that belongs to God, I serve it. Notice this morning, you are a trespasser. You are occupying territory that was purchased with the blood of the son of God. And I command you to vacate. I command healing to come. I command restoration to come. I command vitality to come in the name that broke every yoke in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth. Be healed, be made whole. I pray for those facing financial devastation. For those who cannot see how the numbers will work. For those who have given faithfully and believed faithfully and obeyed and still the lack is screaming louder than the promise. Lord, you are Jehovah Gyra, the Lord who sees and the Lord who provides. You saw Abraham on that mountain. You saw his obedience and you provided in the most unexpected way from the most unexpected direction. Do it again. Do it again. Open windows that no man can shut. Release provision from uncommon sources. Let the wealth of the sinner find its way by divine redirection into the hands of the righteous. Let every blessing that was withheld be released with interest, with compounding heavenly interest into the lives of those who have trusted you through the drought. I pray for marriages, for homes that are fracturing, for relationships that are under siege, for couples who fell asleep loving each other and woke up feeling like strangers. Lord, you are the God [music] who restores. You are the God who said, "I hate divorce." Not because you are a God of rigid rules, but because you are a God who understands what covenant is and what it costs to break it. Lord, let the spirit of restoration move through [music] every marriage under the sound of this prayer. Let the enemy be driven out of the space between husband and wife. Let communication be restored. Let tenderness be restored. Let the love that was there at the beginning come back with a depth and a richness that the years of trial have only deepened. what God has joined together. Let no assignment of hell put us under. I pray for children, for prodigal sons and daughters who have wandered from the faith, from the family, from the values that were planted in them. Lord, you said that when we train [music] up a child in the way he should go, when he is old, he will not depart from it. I stand on that promise for every parent in agony over a child who appears to have departed. Lord, activate the training. Let it arise in them. Let the memory of the altar, the memory of prayer, the memory of truth spoken over them rise up and contend against everything the world has poured into them pull them back. Pull them home. Like the father in the parable who saw the prodigal while he was yet a great way off and ran to meet him. Run to our children. Lord, run to them. Bring them home. I pray against every spirit of death, every premature assignment, every untimely departure that has been scheduled by the enemy for anyone under the sound of this prayer. I decree that they shall live and not die and declare the works of the Lord. Psalm 118, they shall live. The Lord has not appointed them to death but to life. The Lord has not appointed them to failure but to fruitfulness. He has given them a future and a hope, a future of peace and not of evil as declared by the prophet Jeremiah. That word stands this morning. That word is a wall of fire around their lives. And Lord, I pray the specific prayer of Psalm 46. Be still, Lord. In the middle of everything that is roaring and raging and shaking and threatening, command stillness to come into the spirits of those who are hearing this prayer. Command the shaking to stop. Not necessarily in the external circumstances but in the interior of every listener. Let them know Lord that you are God. Not know it intellectually. Not know it historically but know it experientially in their bones in their spirit in the center of their being that you are God. You will be exalted among the nations. You will be exalted in the earth and you will [music] be exalted in their situation. We receive the stillness. We receive the peace. We receive the assurance. The Lord of hosts is with us. The God of Jacob is our refuge. Now, hear me as we close because this is the closing charge and it is not a formality. I want you to take what happened in this moment and I want you to treat it like the treasure that it is. Do not let this word be an experience that makes you feel good for 48 hours and then evaporates. Let it take root. Go back to Psalm 46 today. Not tonight. today. Read it again slowly. Read it with the lens of what the spirit taught you this morning. And then begin to confess it. Begin to declare it over your life with the authority of a son or daughter of the most high. The Lord of hosts is with you. Write it on a piece of paper and put it where you will see it when the fear comes back because it will try to come back. The God of Jacob is your refuge. That is not a bumper sticker. That is your war cry. Carry it into every Monday of every week of every season ahead of you. And remember the dawn is always on the other side of the night. It is always coming. Be still and know that he [music] is God. He will be exalted. And he will be exalted in your life. Go in peace. Go in power. Go in the certainty that the God who never lost a battle is the God who is fighting for you. Amen. Amen. Amen.
